13	#

16	# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,

20	[theme]

```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
23	
24	### Named sessions
25	
26	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
27	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
28	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
29	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
30	
31	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
32	
33	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
34	
35	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
38	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
39	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
40	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
41	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
42	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
43	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
44	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
45	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
46	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
47	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
48	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
49	
50	## Keybindings
51	
52	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
53	
54	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
55	
56	| Key | Action | Type |
57	|---|---|---|
58	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
59	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
60	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
61	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
62	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace nav / session navigator | built-in default |
63	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
64	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
65	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
66	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
67	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
68	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
69	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
70	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
71	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
72	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
73	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
74	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
75	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
76	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
77	
78	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
79	
80	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode`)
81	
82	Two shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion — the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` helpers. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse svibe's pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
83	
84	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
87	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
88	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
89	
90	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
91	- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
92	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
93	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
94	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
95	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
96	
97	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
98	
99	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
100	
101	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
102	
103	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
104	
105	```bash
106	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
107	```
108	
109	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
110	
111	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
112	
113	## Television integration
114	
115	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
116	
117	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
118	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
119	
120	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
121	
122	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
123	
124	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
125	
126	```bash
127	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
128	```
129	
130	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
131	
132	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
133	
134	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
135	
136	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
139	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
140	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
141	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
142	
143	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
144	
145	### Config writeback (why `create_`)
146	
147	herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime. That is why chezmoi manages it as **`create_` (seed-once)**: a plain managed file would be clobbered on every `chezmoi apply` (re-removing `onboarding=false` → the onboarding screen reappears, and reverting any UI change). Consequence: edits to `create_config.toml` in the repo do **not** auto-propagate to a machine that already has the file — refresh it deliberately with `cp ~/.config/herdr/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/herdr/config.toml)"` (then strip the runtime `onboarding`/state lines).
148	
149	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
150	
151	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
152	
153	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
154	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
155	
156	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
157	
158	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
159	
160	```bash
161	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
162	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
163	```
164	
165	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
166	
167	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
168	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
169	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
170	
171	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
172	
173	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
174	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
175	
176	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
177	
178	```bash
179	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
180	```
181	
182	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
183	
184	## AI usage / quota status
185	
186	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into. A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
187	
188	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
189	
190	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
191	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
192	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
193	
194	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
195

1	# chezmoi Source-State Prefixes
2	
3	A practical reference for the filename prefixes (`dot_`, `private_`, `create_`, `modify_`, …) that chezmoi uses to encode target metadata in the source directory, with an opinionated "is it safe to `chezmoi add`?" decision table and a playbook tailored to this repo.
4	
5	## Canonical references
6	
7	- [Source state attributes](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/source-state-attributes/) — full list of prefixes and suffixes, plus the allowed ordering per target type. This is the source of truth; skim it once and bookmark it.
8	- [Manage different types of file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/) — practical recipes, including [Manage part, but not all, of a file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/#manage-part-but-not-all-of-a-file) (the `modify_` pattern) and create-only seeding.
9	- [`chezmoi chattr`](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/commands/chattr/) — toggle prefixes without manually renaming files (e.g. `chezmoi chattr +create,+private ~/.ssh/config`).
10	
11	## `chezmoi add` safety decision table
12	
13	When the live file diverges from the source and you want to resync, the first question is "which bucket does this prefix fall into?". **The prefix changes the semantics of `chezmoi add` / `re-add`** — the command is not a dumb copy.
14	
15	| Bucket | Prefixes | What `chezmoi add <target>` does | Action |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| Green-light | `dot_`, `private_`, `executable_`, `readonly_`, `empty_` | Rewrites the source file with the live contents. Prefixes are preserved. | Use freely. |
18	| Add-safe but re-check semantics | `create_`, `exact_`, `literal_` | Works, but can **silently change the semantic contract** (see notes below). | Use, then `git diff` the source filename to confirm the prefix is still what you expect. |
19	| Do NOT treat as a normal tracked file | `modify_`, `encrypted_`, `remove_`, `symlink_`, scripts (`run_*`) | `chezmoi add` would strip the prefix or overwrite the script body with live data. | Edit the source file directly, or use `cp "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` / `chezmoi edit`. |
20	
21	Notes on the middle bucket:
22	
23	- `create_`: `chezmoi add` **strips** the `create_` prefix, silently promoting a seed-only file to a fully managed one. `chezmoi re-add` is a no-op for `create_` (by design — contents are not managed after initial create).
24	- `exact_` (dir-only): adding a file inside an `exact_` directory is fine, but remember the directory will prune anything not present in source on next apply.
25	- `literal_`: the whole point is to suppress attribute parsing. Adding a new file with the same base name re-parses the prefix — you may need to rename manually.
26	
27	## Per-prefix reference
28	
29	Each entry links to the relevant row in [Source state attributes](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/source-state-attributes/).
30	
31	### `dot_` — leading dot rename
32	
33	- **Effect**: `dot_foo` in source becomes `.foo` in target. Purely a name mapping so dotfiles stay visible in `git ls-files`.
34	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light.
35	- **Typical use**: `dot_zshrc`, `dot_gitconfig`, `dot_config/…`, `dot_ssh/…`.
36	
37	### `private_` — tighten file mode to 0600 (dir: 0700)
38	
39	- **Effect**: Removes group/world permissions on the target. Enforced on every `chezmoi apply`.
40	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light. `chezmoi add` of a file that already has 0600 mode automatically encodes `private_` for you.
41	- **Risk**: This is only a permission bit — it does **not** encrypt the file. Committing a `private_` file with secrets still commits them in plaintext. For secrets, reach for `encrypted_` or a password-manager template function.
42	- **Typical use**: `private_dot_ssh/config`, `private_dot_netrc`, Claude Code config files that contain account hints.
43	
44	### `executable_` — add +x bit
45	
46	- **Effect**: Ensures the target has the executable bit on every apply.
47	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light. Auto-detected when adding a file that already has +x.
48	- **Typical use**: personal scripts under `~/.dotfiles/bin/` (chezmoi-managed; see `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`, `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sms`), helper wrappers, `~/.local/share/tmux-*` shims.
49	
50	### `readonly_` — drop all write bits
51	
52	- **Effect**: Strips write permissions from the target. Runs on every apply, so the file will be reset to read-only even if you `chmod +w` it.
53	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light, but note that re-adding can be annoying because you must `chmod +w` locally first.
54	- **Typical use**: frozen baselines you do not want to edit by mistake. Rarely useful in a personal dotfiles repo.
55	
56	### `create_` — seed once, then leave alone
57	
58	- **Effect**: Writes the file **only if the target does not already exist**. After that, chezmoi never touches the contents again.
59	- **`chezmoi add`**: use with care — `chezmoi add` **strips** the `create_` prefix, which silently promotes the file to a regular managed file (losing the seed-only contract).
60	- **`chezmoi re-add`**: intentionally **skips** `create_` files.
61	- **Refresh recipe**: to update the baseline, copy the live file into the source path (preserves the prefix):
62	
63	  ```bash
64	  cp ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json)"
65	  ```
66	
67	- **Typical use**: LazyVim `lazy-lock.json` (see the [case study below](#dot_confignvimcreate_lazy-lockjson--seed-once-never-overwrite)), SSH `config` skeleton, first-run app baselines.
68	
69	### `modify_` — content is a script, not a file
70	
71	- **Effect**: The source file is an executable **script**. chezmoi pipes the current target contents into stdin; the script writes the new target contents to stdout. Lets you manage part of a file (e.g. via `jq`, `sed`, `awk`) while leaving the rest alone.
72	- **`chezmoi add`**: do **not** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite your script with the live file contents.
73	- **Alternative form**: put `chezmoi:modify-template` in the script body to switch it into template mode (the current contents arrive as `.chezmoi.stdin`). See [Manage part, but not all, of a file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/#manage-part-but-not-all-of-a-file).
74	- **Typical use**: Claude Code `settings.json` (see the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq)), Docker `config.json` proxies, INI files with a mix of managed and runtime-written keys.
75	
76	#### Bootstrap-order contract: `modify_` scripts MUST tolerate missing tools
77	
78	`chezmoi apply` runs in three phases, in order:
79	
80	1. `run_once_before_*` scripts → `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` installs **uv, mise, ansible-core**, plus Linuxbrew (rooted Linux) or Homebrew (macOS). It assumes `curl`, `git`, `bash`/`sh`, and basic POSIX are already on the box.
81	2. **File-application phase** — every `modify_*` script runs here.
82	3. `run_onchange_after_*` scripts → `20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` runs the `base` ansible role, which installs **`jq`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `python3`, `git-lfs`, `just`, `tree`, …**.
83	
84	So at the time a `modify_*` script executes, **only the bootstrap-set is guaranteed**. Anything from the ansible-set (`jq`, `python3`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, …) may not yet be installed on a fresh box. A bare `set -eu` script that hard-calls one of those tools will exit non-zero, and chezmoi will abort the entire apply — meaning the ansible role that *would have* installed the tool never runs, and the user is stuck.
85	
86	**Rule**: any `modify_*` script that invokes a tool from the post-bootstrap set MUST `command -v`-guard it and pass-through the live content if missing. The pass-through preserves the live file unchanged (chezmoi sees `stdout == stdin` → no-op for that target → apply continues), and the next `chezmoi apply` (after ansible has installed the missing tool) does the real work.
87	
88	Canonical guard, lifted from [`run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl:32-35`](../../.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl):
89	
90	```sh
91	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
92	  printf '%s\n' "modify_<file>: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
93	  printf '%s' "$base"
94	  exit 0
95	fi
96	```
97	
98	For scripts needing a python3 (e.g. JSONC handling for VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity overlays), prefer the uv→system-python3 fallback chain — `uv` is bootstrap-guaranteed, so it's the cheap insurance against minimal Linux servers without `python3` pre-installed. See [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl:47-55`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) and [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh:48-66`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh) for the pattern.
99	
100	Reference implementations (good citizens worth copying):
101	
102	- [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl:47-55`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) — `uv` → `python3` → pass-through
103	- [`dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl:28-31`](../../dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl) — minimal `jq` guard
104	- [`dot_docker/modify_config.json.tmpl:19-21`](../../dot_docker/modify_config.json.tmpl) — minimal `jq` guard
105	
106	Failure mode if the rule is forgotten: see [`pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md) — `chezmoi update --init` aborts with `jq: command not found` after `[SUCCESS] Bootstrap complete!` and the user is stuck in a cycle (apply fails before phase 3 → ansible never runs → `jq` never installs → next apply fails the same way).
107	
108	### `exact_` — directory is canonical (prune extras)
109	
110	- **Effect**: On apply, chezmoi **removes** any file inside the target directory that is not present in source. Directory-only prefix.
111	- **`chezmoi add`**: safe for individual files inside the directory, but be aware of the semantic trap — next apply will clean up anything that drifted in.
112	- **Risk**: Very easy to accidentally delete machine-local artifacts (caches, plugin installs) that happen to live inside the directory.
113	- **Typical use**: directories you truly own end-to-end and that are small / stable. Avoid for any directory that mixes managed config with runtime state.
114	
115	### `literal_` — stop parsing attributes
116	
117	- **Effect**: Tells chezmoi to stop interpreting the rest of the filename as attributes. Used when an actual filename starts with something like `create` or `run` and you want chezmoi to treat it literally.
118	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light, but remember the prefix exists for a filename-level reason — blindly renaming it later can break the mapping.
119	- **Typical use**: uncommon. Corner cases like a literal `run_` or `dot_` in a filename.
120	
121	### `remove_` — assert removal
122	
123	- **Effect**: Declares that the target should be **absent**. On apply, chezmoi removes the file/symlink (or empty directory) if it exists. The source file's body is not a content source — it is a presence assertion.
124	- **`chezmoi add`**: does not apply (there is no live content to sync back).
125	- **Typical use**: cleaning up stale configs after migrating tools. Often combined with a template so it only fires on specific hosts.
126	
127	### `encrypted_` — encrypt at rest
128	
129	- **Effect**: The source file is stored encrypted (age or gpg, depending on `encryption` config). chezmoi decrypts on apply. The on-disk suffix is `.age` or `.asc` (stripped in the target).
130	- **`chezmoi add`**: supported (chezmoi re-encrypts), but this only makes sense if you have already committed to a secrets workflow (age keys, gpg setup).
131	- **Alternative**: use a template function (`onepassword`, `bitwarden`, `keyring`, `vault`, …) to fetch secrets at apply time instead of committing them encrypted.
132	- **Typical use**: small number of credential files you want to keep inside the repo history.
133	
134	### `symlink_` — create a symlink, not a file
135	
136	- **Effect**: Target is a symlink whose contents are the first line of the source file (often a template that expands to a path).
137	- **`chezmoi add`**: adding an existing symlink produces a `symlink_` source automatically.
138	- **Typical use**: point a dotfile at an externally-managed file (`~/.config/Code/User/settings.json` → `{{ .chezmoi.sourceDir }}/settings.json`, see the official recipe for handling externally-modified configs).
139	
140	### `empty_` — allow empty files
141	
142	- **Effect**: By default chezmoi removes zero-byte files; `empty_` says "this one is intentionally empty".
143	- **Typical use**: marker files, empty `.hushlogin`.
144	
145	### `external_` — don't parse attributes of children
146	
147	- **Effect**: Directory-only. Stops chezmoi from interpreting the attributes of files inside. Usually paired with `.chezmoiexternal.<format>` sources that deliver whole subtrees.
148	- **Typical use**: vendored plugin directories, `git-repo` externals.
149	- **Companion file**: `.chezmoiexternal.<format>` at the repo root (see [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` in this repo](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) and the section below).
150	
151	### Script family — `run_`, `once_`, `onchange_`, `before_`, `after_`
152	
153	- **Effect**: Source file is a **script** that chezmoi executes at apply time. No target file is created. The modifiers compose:
154	  - `run_` — the base marker.
155	  - `once_` — run only once per script body (hash-keyed).
156	  - `onchange_` — run when the script body changes (filename-keyed; unlike `once_`, editing the script re-runs it).
157	  - `before_` / `after_` — run before / after applying target files.
158	- **`chezmoi add`**: does not apply — scripts have no file target.
159	- **Already in this repo**: `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`. See [docs/this_repo/architecture.md → Auto-run scripts](../this_repo/architecture.md#auto-run-scripts).
160	
161	## Allowed prefix ordering
162	
163	When multiple prefixes apply, order matters. From [Source state attributes](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/source-state-attributes/):
164	
165	| Target type | Allowed prefixes (in order) | Allowed suffixes |
166	|---|---|---|
167	| Directory | `remove_`, `external_`, `exact_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `dot_` | — |
168	| Regular file | `encrypted_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `empty_`, `executable_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
169	| Create file | `create_`, `encrypted_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `empty_`, `executable_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
170	| Modify file | `modify_`, `encrypted_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `executable_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
171	| Remove file | `remove_`, `dot_` | — |
172	| Script | `run_`, (`once_` or `onchange_`), (`before_` or `after_`) | `.tmpl` |
173	| Symlink | `symlink_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
174	
175	Worked examples:
176	
177	- `private_executable_dot_ssh/private_readonly_id_ed25519` — directory is private, file is private+readonly. (In practice: don't check in private keys; shown for ordering only.)
178	- `create_private_dot_ssh/create_private_config` — create-once SSH config that is 0600 on creation.
179	- `modify_private_dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — the actual pattern used in this repo (see the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq)).
180	
181	If you ever lose the stacking order, `chezmoi chattr` will normalize it for you:
182	
183	```bash
184	chezmoi chattr +private,+readonly ~/.config/foo/bar
185	```
186	
187	## Playbook: what to use where in this repo
188	
189	### A. Everyday configs — `dot_` (+ `private_` if sensitive)
190	
191	Track normally, `chezmoi add` freely, let `chezmoi re-add` pick up drift.
192	
193	- `dot_zshrc`, `dot_gitconfig`, `dot_tmux.conf`, `dot_config/nvim/lua/*`, `dot_config/starship.toml`, `dot_config/tmux/*`, `dot_config/zsh/tools/*`, `dot_config/sesh/*`, `dot_config/zellij/*`, …
194	- Sensitive-ish (account hints, but not secrets): add `private_` (e.g. `private_dot_ssh/…`, `private_dot_claude/…`).
195	
196	### B. Personal scripts — `executable_` (+ `dot_` where needed)
197	
198	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` → `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sms` in source.
199	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` → `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` in source.
200	- Any helper shell script you want on PATH — drop it under `dot_dotfiles/bin/` with the `executable_` prefix.
201	
202	### C. Seed-once baselines — `create_`
203	
204	Files that an app rewrites in-place after first launch, and where you only care about the initial state.
205	
206	- **`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`** → `create_lazy-lock.json`. See the [case study below](#dot_confignvimcreate_lazy-lockjson--seed-once-never-overwrite). Refresh baseline with `cp … "$(chezmoi source-path …)"`.
207	- **`~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** → `create_config.toml`. herdr writes UI/runtime settings back into it (`onboarding = false`, theme/sound/toasts on *apply*), so a plain managed file would be clobbered every `chezmoi apply` (re-triggering onboarding). See [docs/tools/herdr.md → Config writeback](herdr.md#config-writeback-why-create_).
208	- **`~/.ssh/config`** → create-only template that `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` and ships conservative defaults. See the SSH notes in [README.md](../../README.md).
209	- First-run app JSONs where further changes are user-local (settings files that are a mix of state and preferences).
210	
211	### D. Partial-content management — `modify_` via script
212	
213	Files an app actively rewrites at runtime (adding keys, reordering, …), where you only want to enforce a subset of keys.
214	
215	- **`~/.claude/settings.json`** → `dot_claude/modify_settings.json`, a `jq` script that deep-merges a managed overlay. See the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq).
216	- **`~/.docker/config.json`** → a modify-script that rewrites `proxies.default` while preserving `auths` / `credsStore`. See [docs/tools/containers.md](containers.md).
217	- Rule of thumb: if an app owns the file and you only care about N keys, `modify_` beats a full managed template.
218	
219	### E. Machine-local / runtime / cache — `.chezmoiignore`, not a prefix
220	
221	Do **not** try to track these even with `create_`. They belong in `.chezmoiignore` or simply outside the source tree.
222	
223	- Editor swap / shada / session files
224	- Plugin install artifacts (LazyVim plugin source, tmux TPM repos, …)
225	- Logs, caches, `lazy-install.log`, `.DS_Store`
226	- Per-host runtime state
227	
228	### F. Secrets — prefer templating over `encrypted_`
229	
230	Order of preference for secrets in this repo:
231	
232	1. **Template function** that fetches at apply-time: `{{ bitwarden … }}`, `{{ onepassword … }}`, `{{ keyring … }}`, `{{ vault … }}`. Nothing secret hits git.
233	2. **`encrypted_`** with age or gpg, if you need the value in-repo (e.g. for an offline machine). Commit only after you have `encryption` set and a key workflow in place.
234	3. **Never** commit a plain `private_` file with a real token — `private_` is a permission bit, not encryption.
235	
236	## Refresh / maintenance recipes
237	
238	### `chezmoi re-add` vs `chezmoi add`
239	
240	| Situation | Command |
241	|---|---|
242	| File already tracked, just pick up drift | `chezmoi re-add <target>` (preserves prefix, fails loudly on `modify_`, silently skips `create_`) |
243	| Adding a new file for the first time | `chezmoi add <target>` |
244	| Updating a `create_` baseline | `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` |
245	| Updating a `modify_` script | Edit the source script directly (`chezmoi edit <target>`) |
246	| Changing prefixes on an existing source file | `chezmoi chattr +create,+private <target>` (or `-executable`, etc.) |
247	
248	### Preview before committing
249	
250	```bash
251	chezmoi diff <target>           # See target diff
252	chezmoi apply --dry-run -v      # See what would happen on this machine
253	chezmoi status                  # Which files are in A/M/D state
254	```
255	
256	### When `chezmoi add` seems to have "done the wrong thing"
257	
258	Most often the prefix was silently stripped:
259	
260	```bash
261	chezmoi source-path <target>    # Where does it live?
262	ls "$(dirname "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)")"  # Inspect neighbors — did the prefix disappear?
263	chezmoi chattr +create <target> # Put it back
264	```
265	
266	For a `modify_` target, rewind the script from git:
267	
268	```bash
269	git -C "$(chezmoi source-path)" checkout -- <relative/path/to/modify_file>
270	```
271	
272	## Companion file: `.chezmoiexternal.<format>`
273	
274	Not a prefix, but a repo-level companion mechanism: a single declarative file at the repo root that tells chezmoi to fetch upstream content (git repos, single files, archives) into the target tree. Reference: [Include files from elsewhere](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/include-files-from-elsewhere/) and [`.chezmoiexternal.<format>` reference](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/special-files-and-directories/chezmoiexternal-format/).
275	
276	### In this repo: [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
277	
278	Source of truth for upstream clones that used to live in ansible roles. Entries today:
279	
280	| Target | Type | URL | Previously in |
281	|---|---|---|---|
282	| `~/.oh-my-zsh` | `git-repo` | `ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
283	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions` | `git-repo` | `zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
284	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-syntax-highlighting` | `git-repo` | `zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
285	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions` | `git-repo` | `zsh-users/zsh-completions` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
286	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` | `git-repo` | `jeffreytse/zsh-vi-mode` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` (gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode`, default true; see [vim-mode.md](../this_repo/vim-mode.md)) |
287	| `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm` | `git-repo` | `tmux-plugins/tpm` | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools` |
288	| `~/.fzf` (Linux only) | `git-repo` | `junegunn/fzf` | `dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps` |
289	| `~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb` | `file` | `aperoc/toolkami/main/toolkami.rb` | `dot_ansible/roles/ruby_gem_tools` |
290	
291	All `git-repo` entries use `--depth 1` and `--ff-only` on pull; all entries have `refreshPeriod = "168h"` (weekly auto-refresh).
292	
293	### How updates propagate
294	
295	```bash
296	chezmoi apply                 # normal cadence: checks refreshPeriod,
297	                              # pulls upstream only when older than 168h
298	chezmoi apply --refresh-externals   # force: pull every external now
299	```
300	
301	Externals are evaluated **before** `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`, so by the time ansible runs, `~/.oh-my-zsh`, `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`, `~/.fzf`, and `~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb` already exist. Ansible's remaining responsibilities for these tools:
302	
303	- `zsh` role: install the `zsh` package + change login shell (sudo).
304	- `devtools` role: run `tpm/bin/install_plugins` once (sentinel at `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed`).
305	- `lazyvim_deps` role: run `~/.fzf/install --bin` (idempotent via `creates: ~/.fzf/bin/fzf`).
306	
307	### Nested externals
308	
309	`.oh-my-zsh` and `.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/<name>` are both declared as separate `git-repo` externals. chezmoi does `git pull` on refresh (not re-clone), so the subdirectories are preserved across refreshes — this is the standard oh-my-zsh install pattern.
310	
311	### When to add an entry here vs. keep it in ansible
312	
313	Good fit for `.chezmoiexternal`:
314	
315	- Plain git clone or single-file download, no arch / OS logic other than `.chezmoi.os` conditional.
316	- No post-clone build step (or the build step is idempotent and lives in ansible).
317	- You want the upstream pulled automatically on a schedule.
318	
319	Keep in ansible:
320	
321	- Conditional arch / `noRoot` / `armv7l` skip logic (GitHub release binaries).
322	- Clones whose destination path contains a dynamic version (e.g. `claude-hud` uses `v<tag>` in path and writes `installed_plugins.json`).
323	- Anything that needs `become: true` after the clone.
324	
325	### Editing workflow
326	
327	1. Add / remove entries in `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`.
328	2. `chezmoi diff` — verify no unexpected target diffs (externals don't show per-file diff; you'll see the TOML change).
329	3. `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` — fetch and apply.
330	4. If you removed an entry, chezmoi does **not** delete the destination directory (it's not managed anymore). Remove it manually if you want a clean state.
331	
332	## Case studies in this repo
333	
334	Three concrete walkthroughs of the `modify_` / `create_` patterns above, with the failure modes that bit us.
335	
336	### `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — partial JSON management via jq
337	
338	Claude Code rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` at runtime (adds `permissions`, `skipAutoPermissionPrompt`, reorders keys). A static managed file would produce diff on every apply.
339	
340	`modify_` files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents into stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. The script uses `jq '. * $overlay'` to deep-merge a managed overlay over the live file:
341	
342	- Keys in the overlay are enforced by chezmoi: `hooks`, `enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, `statusLine`.
343	- Any other keys Claude Code adds (model, permissions, `skipAutoPermissionPrompt`, etc.) are preserved verbatim.
344	- Arrays in the overlay replace their counterparts wholesale, so `hooks.Notification` won't accumulate duplicates.
345	
346	To manage an additional key, add it to the `overlay` heredoc in `dot_claude/modify_settings.json`. Requires `jq` (installed by the `base` ansible role). The source file must have exec bit set (git mode `100755`).
347	
348	**Failure mode**: if the live `~/.claude/settings.json` contains invalid JSON (e.g. Claude Code writes a stray trailing comma), `jq` aborts with a parse error and the script exits non-zero. chezmoi then logs `chezmoi: .claude/settings.json: exit status 5` and skips the file for that apply; the broken live file is left untouched for manual inspection. No partial / corrupt output is ever written. Fix or delete the live file and re-run `chezmoi apply`.
349	
350	### `.chezmoitemplates/editor/*` — shared overlay for VSCode / Cursor / Antigravity
351	
352	All three Electron editors read `settings.json` + `keybindings.json` from a per-editor `User/` directory (macOS `~/Library/Application Support/<Editor>/User/`, Linux `~/.config/<Editor>/User/`). Three concerns we manage cross-editor, cross-OS, without fighting each editor's own writes:
353	
354	1. A tiny **universal baseline** (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart accept-suggestion, terminal font) — canonical in [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json). Add a key here and it deploys to all six targets (3 editors × 2 OSes).
355	2. **Keybindings** that should seed on a fresh machine but never overwrite an editor's own additions (e.g. Cursor's `alt+cmd+s`) — canonical in [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/keybindings.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/keybindings.json).
356	3. The `modify_` / `create_` plumbing itself — the bash+python+jq merge script lives once in [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh); each of the 6 per-editor wrappers is a 1-line `{{ template … }}` shim.
357	
358	`modify_settings.json.tmpl` uses an inline Python JSONC normaliser (strip `//` and `/* */` comments + trailing commas) before piping into `jq '. * $overlay'`. This is the only place in the repo where live JSONC needs to be deep-merged in-place; **do not duplicate the script** — extend [`modify.sh`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh) if you need a new overlay section (e.g. `[python]` block overrides).
359	
360	`create_keybindings.json.tmpl` is seed-once. To push an updated baseline to an existing live file, copy the live file back into the source path (`cp ~/Library/Application\ Support/Code/User/keybindings.json "$(chezmoi source-path ...)"`) to fold in editor-added entries, then edit the template.
361	
362	**Presence gating in [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl).** It ignores both halves of the cross-OS tree on the wrong OS (`Library/**` on non-darwin, `.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/**` on non-linux), then per-editor `stat` gates ignore the whole subtree when the editor's config dir does not exist. Net effect: a fresh machine with only VSCode installed gets Code settings + skips Cursor/Antigravity entirely, no phantom directories. The `private_` prefix on `Library`, `Application Support`, and each editor dir preserves macOS's native `0700`/`0755` mode.
363	
364	When adding a fourth editor (e.g. Zed if it ever adopts the same layout), drop it into the `range (list "Code" "Cursor" "Antigravity" "NewEditor")` list in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` and mirror the 4 source files (`{modify_settings,create_keybindings}.json.tmpl` × macOS/Linux).
365	
366	### `dot_config/nvim/create_lazy-lock.json` — seed-once, never overwrite
367	
368	LazyVim rewrites `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` on every `:Lazy update` and the tracked plugin list differs across OSes. `create_` only writes when the target file does not yet exist (new-machine seed), so subsequent edits produce zero chezmoi diff.
369	
370	**Refreshing the baseline after a deliberate plugin bump.** Neither `chezmoi re-add` nor `chezmoi add` is the right tool here:
371	
372	- `chezmoi re-add` silently **skips** `create_` files (by design — `create_` means contents are not managed).
373	- `chezmoi add` would **strip** the `create_` prefix, promoting it to a plain managed file (defeating the whole point).
374	
375	Instead, copy the live file directly into the source path (this preserves the prefix):
376	
377	```bash
378	cp ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json)"
379	```
380	
381	This is an explicit, opt-in step instead of constant apply noise.
382	
383	## See also
384	
385	- [docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md → chezmoi](../this_repo/cheatsheet.md#chezmoi) — command-level quick reference.
386	- [chezmoi docs — Concepts](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/concepts/) — source state vs destination state vs target state.
387	- [chezmoi docs — Include files from elsewhere](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/include-files-from-elsewhere/) — `.chezmoiexternal.<format>` user guide.
388
```
</details></tool-use>

docs/tools/herdr.md:54:> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
docs/tools/herdr.md:60:| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
docs/tools/herdr.md:92:- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
docs/tools/herdr.md:93:- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
docs/tools/herdr.md:94:- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
docs/tools/herdr.md:117:- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
docs/tools/herdr.md:190:- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.

90	    "Link to session..." K { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "link-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%:'" } \
91	    "Break all panes → windows" E { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh" } \
92	    "" \
93	    "Kill window" X { kill-window } \
94	    "Renumber windows" N { move-window -r ; display-message "Windows renumbered" } \
95	    "Rename"      n { command-prompt -F -I "#W" { rename-window -t "#{window_id}" "%%" } } \
96	    "" \
97	    "⭐ Star"     s { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '⭐'" } \
98	    "📌 Pin"      p { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '📌'" } \
99	    "🔖 Bookmark" b { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🔖'" } \
100	    "🚩 Flag"     f { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🚩'" } \
101	    "Clear agent status" c { set-option -w -t "#{window_id}" -u "@workmux_status" ; display-message "Cleared @workmux_status on #{window_index}:#{window_name}" } \
102	    "" \
103	    "New window"  w { new-window }
104	
105	unbind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft
106	# *** IF YOU EDIT THE MENU BODY, ALSO UPDATE dot_config/tmux/menu-status-left.sh ***
107	# (keyboard equivalent is `prefix + M-s`; body duplicated by design — see the
108	# comment above MouseDown3Pane for the pitfall reference.)
109	#
110	# "Kill all sessions (clean)" + "Kill session & exit" route through the clean-quit
111	# helpers so tmux-continuum does NOT auto-restore the just-closed sessions.
112	# See pitfalls/tmux-continuum-restores-on-intentional-quit.md.
113	bind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft \
114	  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{session_name}" -t = -x M -y W \
115	    Next        n { switch-client -n } \
116	    Previous    p { switch-client -p } \
117	    "" \
118	    "Choose session..." c { choose-tree -Zs } \
119	    Rename      N { command-prompt -I "#S" { rename-session "%%" } } \
120	    "Copy session name" y { set-buffer -w "#{session_name}" ; display-message "Copied session name: #{session_name}" } \
121	    "" \
122	    "Move current window to..." m { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'" } \
123	    "" \
124	    "New session" s { new-session } \
125	    "New window"  w { new-window } \
126	    "" \
127	    "Kill session"        X { kill-session } \
128	    "Kill session & exit" E { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh" } \
129	    "Kill all sessions (clean)" Q { confirm-before -p "Kill ALL sessions cleanly (forget auto-restore)? (y/n)" "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/kill-server-clean.sh'" } \
130	    "Forget auto-restore" F { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/resurrect-forget.sh" ; display-message "Forgot tmux auto-restore snapshot" }
