132	# =============================================================================
133	# Vim-Style Copy Mode (prefix + [ to enter, q to exit)
134	# =============================================================================
135	#
136	#   h/j/k/l  move cursor        C-u/C-d  half-page up/down
137	#   g/G      top/bottom          //?      search forward/backward
138	#   v        begin selection     V        line selection
139	#   C-v      rectangle select    y        yank to clipboard
140	#   Escape   clear selection     q        exit copy mode
141	
142	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} v send-keys -X begin-selection
143	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} V send-keys -X select-line
144	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} C-v send-keys -X rectangle-toggle
145	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} y send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
146	# Mouse drag = select-only (vim visual feel): highlight without copying, then `y`
147	# (copy-selection-and-cancel above) copies + exits. `stop-selection` keeps the
148	# highlight alive without leaving copy-mode. See docs/tools/tmux/.
149	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X stop-selection
150	# Double-click selects the word AND copies + exits (one gesture).
151	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word \; send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
152	
153	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
154	# Command-boundary navigation in copy-mode (Warp-style).
155	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by
156	# dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh. In a plain shell (no markers,
157	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
158	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
159	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
160	#
161	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
162	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
163	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
164	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
166	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
167	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
168	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o
169	
170	# =============================================================================
171	# Capture Pane Helpers
172	# =============================================================================
173	
174	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
175	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
176	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
177	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
178	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
179	
180	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
181	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"
182	
183	# prefix + C-y: capture pane into fzf for line-by-line selection, yank chosen lines
184	bind C-y run-shell "\
185	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
186	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
187	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
188	
189	# prefix + C-p: copy the current pane's path (session:window.pane) to clipboard.
190	# (Capital P is taken by tmux-floax's scratchpad; lowercase p is previous-window.)
191	# Handy for reconnecting later or telling an AI agent which pane to operate on
192	# (`tmux capture-pane -pt <target>` / `tmux send-keys -t <target> ...`). Same
193	# keyboard equivalent lives in the MouseDown3Pane right-click menu and menu-pane.sh.
194	bind C-p run-shell "tmux set-buffer -w \"#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\" ; tmux display-message \"Copied pane path: #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\""
195	
196	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
197	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
198	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
199	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
200	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
201	# flash confirmation.
202	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
203	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
204	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
205	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
206	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
207	  display-message "Last command output copied to clipboard"
208	
209	# prefix + M-i: copy the LAST command's INPUT LINE (prompt + typed command).
210	# Same dependency on OSC 133 markers. Because we don't emit the B marker
211	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
212	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
213	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
214	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
215	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
216	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
217	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
218	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
219	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
220	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
221	
222	# =============================================================================
223	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
224	# =============================================================================
225	
226	bind h select-pane -L
227	bind j select-pane -D
228	bind k select-pane -U
229	bind l select-pane -R
230	
231	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
232	# vim-tmux-navigator: prefix-less Ctrl+h/j/k/l crosses tmux panes <-> vim splits
233	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
234	# Detect if the current pane is running vim/neovim; if so forward the key,
235	# otherwise move between tmux panes. Matches christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator.
236	# Gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` (default true). When off, Ctrl+h/j/k/l
237	# pass through to the inner shell (Ctrl+L = clear, Ctrl+H = backspace, etc.).
238	# See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.
239	{{ if .enableVimMode -}}
240	is_vim="ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'"
241	bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-h'  'select-pane -L'
242	bind-key -n 'C-j' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-j'  'select-pane -D'
243	bind-key -n 'C-k' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-k'  'select-pane -U'
244	bind-key -n 'C-l' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-l'  'select-pane -R'
245	# NOTE: C-\ (select-pane -l) removed — tmux 3.4+ cannot parse C-\ in config files.
246	# Use directional C-h/j/k/l instead, or prefix+; for last-pane.
247	
248	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-h' select-pane -L
249	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-j' select-pane -D
250	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-k' select-pane -U
251	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-l' select-pane -R
252	{{- else -}}
253	# enableVimMode = false: vim-tmux-navigator omitted. Use prefix + h/j/k/l
254	# (kept below) or prefix + Arrow for pane navigation.
255	{{- end }}
256	
257	# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
258	bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
259	bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
260	
261	# Also override default % and " so they inherit current pane's cwd (consistent with | / - and `c`)
262	bind % split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
263	bind '"' split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
264	
265	# Resize panes with prefix + H/J/K/L (5 cells)
266	bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
267	bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
268	bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
269	bind -r L resize-pane -R 5
270	
271	# Fine resize with Meta + h/j/k/l (1 cell, repeatable)
272	bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
273	bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
274	bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
275	bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1
276	
277	# Quick ratio: set current pane to 75% width
278	bind + resize-pane -x 75%
279	
280	# =============================================================================
281	# Quick Window Switching (Ctrl+Number, requires CSI-u / extended-keys)
282	# =============================================================================
283	# Supplement to prefix + 1..9 (tmux built-in defaults, always available).
284	# These require extended-keys (CSI-u) support from the terminal emulator
285	# (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty, WezTerm). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app,
286	# plain SSH) will not send these sequences — use prefix + number instead.
287	# Note: prefix + 9 / prefix + 0 are rebound below (scode / sesh-root for
288	# current dir), so Ctrl+9 below is the only way to reach window 9 from
289	# the keyboard. Ctrl+0 mirrors prefix+0 (lightweight sesh-root) since
290	# base-index is 1 and window 0 doesn't exist.
291	
292	bind-key -n C-1 select-window -t :=1
293	bind-key -n C-2 select-window -t :=2
294	bind-key -n C-3 select-window -t :=3
295	bind-key -n C-4 select-window -t :=4
296	bind-key -n C-5 select-window -t :=5
297	bind-key -n C-6 select-window -t :=6
298	bind-key -n C-7 select-window -t :=7
299	bind-key -n C-8 select-window -t :=8
300	bind-key -n C-9 select-window -t :=9
301	bind-key -n C-0 run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
302	
303	# New window/pane inherits current path
304	bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
305	
306	# Reload config with prefix + R
307	bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"
308	
309	# Session management
310	bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
311	bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
312	# Kill current session AND detach client (return to parent shell).
313	# Differs from `prefix + X` above, which keeps you inside tmux by
314	# switching to another session (detach-on-destroy off, common.conf).
315	# Chained via helper script because `confirm-before` takes a single
316	# tmux command; inline `\;` inside its string arg is not parsed as a
317	# command separator.
318	bind M-x confirm-before -p "Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)" \
319	  "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
320	bind M-Q confirm-before -p "Kill ALL sessions cleanly (forget auto-restore)? (y/n)" \
321	  "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-server-clean.sh'"
322	bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane
323	bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
324	
325	# Manual renumber (renumber-windows on usually handles this, but kill-pane on
326	# multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can leave gaps).
327	bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
328	
329	# =============================================================================
330	# Move/Break Windows Across Sessions (GUI tab tear-out feel)
331	# =============================================================================
332	# prefix + M : move current window to another session (interactive prompt).
333	#              Target form: "session:" (auto-pick index) or "session:index"
334	#              (use -k via "!session:index" trick? simpler: bare prompt).
335	#              Tab-completes existing sessions.
336	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
337	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
338	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
339	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
340	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
341	#
342	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
343	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
344	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
345	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
346	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
347	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
348	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
349	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
350	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
351	
352	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
353	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
354	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
355	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
356	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
357	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
358	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
359	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
360	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
361	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
362	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
363	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
364	
365	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
366	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
367	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
368	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
369	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
370	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
371	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
372	
373	# =============================================================================
374	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
375	# =============================================================================
376	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
377	
378	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
379	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
380	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
381	
382	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
383	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
384	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
385	
386	# =============================================================================
387	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
388	# =============================================================================
389	
390	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
391	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
392	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
393	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
394	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
395	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
396	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
397	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
398	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
399	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
400	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
401	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
402	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
403	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
404	)\""
405	
406	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
407	
408	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
409	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
410	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
411	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
412	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
413	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
414	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
415	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
416	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
417	
418	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
419	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
420	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
421	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
422	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
423	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
424	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
425	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
426	
427	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
428	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
429	
430	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
431	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
432	
433	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
434	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
435	
436	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
437	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
438	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
439	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
440	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
441	
442	# prefix + M-a: quota/rate-limit wakeup dashboard for live agent panes.
443	# Shows quota waits, parsed reset times, and pueue-scheduled continue tasks.
444	bind-key M-a display-popup -E -w 88% -h 75% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Agent wakeup (tv) ' "tv agent-wakeup"
445	
446	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
447	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
448	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
449	
450	# =============================================================================
451	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
452	# =============================================================================
453	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
454	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
455	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
456	# the layout" workflows.
457	
458	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
459	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
460	
461	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
462	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
463	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
464	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
465	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
466	
467	# =============================================================================
468	# Help / cheatsheet
469	# =============================================================================
470	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
471	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
472	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
473	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
474	#
475	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
476	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
477	#
478	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
479	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
480	
481	unbind-key '?'
482	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
483	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
484	
485	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
486	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
487	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
488	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
489	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
490	
491	# =============================================================================
492	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
493	# =============================================================================
494	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
495	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
496	#
497	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
498	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
499	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
500	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
501	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
502	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
503	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
504	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
505	#
506	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
507	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
508	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
509	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
510	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
511	#
512	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
513	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
514	# right-click on a pane / status line.
515	
516	unbind-key Space
517	unbind-key Enter
518	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
519	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
520	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
521	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
522	# in the window right-click menu).
523	
524	# =============================================================================
525	# Right-click menus on the keyboard (prefix + M-p / M-w / M-s)
526	# =============================================================================
527	# Keyboard equivalents of the three MouseDown3* right-click menus defined at
528	# the top of this file:
529	#
530	#   prefix + M-p  →  menu-pane.sh         (same as right-click on a pane)
531	#   prefix + M-w  →  menu-window.sh       (same as right-click on a window tab)
532	#   prefix + M-s  →  menu-status-left.sh  (same as right-click on the session
533	#                                          name in the status-left area)
534	#
535	# WHY scripts (not inline `display-menu` like the MouseDown3* bindings):
536	# `pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md` — a `display-menu` launched
537	# indirectly via `run-shell` from a MouseDown3 binding has its mouse-release
538	# event leaked into the menu, dismissing it instantly. So the MouseDown3*
539	# bodies MUST stay inline above. Keyboard activation has no pending mouse
540	# event, so a script wrapper is safe — and keeps this file shorter. The menu
541	# bodies are duplicated between the MouseDown3* bindings here and the scripts
542	# under dot_config/tmux/menu-*.sh; each location carries a "sync me" comment.
543	#
544	# Requires terminal Option-as-Meta on macOS (already set by the repo's
545	# Ghostty/cmux config: `macos-option-as-alt = left`). On Linux terminals the
546	# Alt modifier is sent natively.
547	
548	bind -N "right-click pane menu (keyboard)"      M-p run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-pane.sh"
549	bind -N "right-click window menu (keyboard)"    M-w run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-window.sh"
550	bind -N "right-click status-left menu (keyboard)" M-s run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-status-left.sh"
551

```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
23	
24	### Named sessions
25	
26	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
27	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
28	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
29	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
30	
31	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
32	
33	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
34	
35	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
38	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
39	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
40	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
41	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
42	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
43	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
44	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
45	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
46	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
47	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
48	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
49	
50	## Keybindings
51	
52	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
53	
54	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
55	
56	| Key | Action | Type |
57	|---|---|---|
58	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
59	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
60	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
61	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
62	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace nav / session navigator | built-in default |
63	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
64	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
65	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
66	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
67	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
68	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
69	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
70	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
71	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
72	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
73	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
74	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
75	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
76	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
77	
78	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
79	
80	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode`)
81	
82	Two shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion — the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` helpers. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse svibe's pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
83	
84	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
87	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
88	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
89	
90	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
91	- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
92	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
93	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
94	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
95	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
96	
97	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
98	
99	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
100	
101	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
102	
103	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
104	
105	```bash
106	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
107	```
108	
109	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
110	
111	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
112	
113	## Television integration
114	
115	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
116	
117	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
118	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
119	
120	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
121	
122	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
123	
124	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
125	
126	```bash
127	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
128	```
129	
130	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
131	
132	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
133	
134	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
135	
136	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
139	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
140	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
141	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
142	
143	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
144	
145	### Config writeback (why `create_`)
146	
147	herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime. That is why chezmoi manages it as **`create_` (seed-once)**: a plain managed file would be clobbered on every `chezmoi apply` (re-removing `onboarding=false` → the onboarding screen reappears, and reverting any UI change). Consequence: edits to `create_config.toml` in the repo do **not** auto-propagate to a machine that already has the file — refresh it deliberately with `cp ~/.config/herdr/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/herdr/config.toml)"` (then strip the runtime `onboarding`/state lines).
148	
149	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
150	
151	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
152	
153	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
154	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
155	
156	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
157	
158	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
159	
160	```bash
161	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
162	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
163	```
164	
165	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
166	
167	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
168	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
169	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
170	
171	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
172	
173	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
174	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
175	
176	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
177	
178	```bash
179	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
180	```
181	
182	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
183	
184	## AI usage / quota status
185	
186	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into. A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
187	
188	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
189	
190	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
191	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
192	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
193	
194	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
195	
196	## See also
197	
198	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
199	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
200

170	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
171	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
172	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
173	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
174	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
175	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
176	
177	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
178	
179	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
180	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
181	
182	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
183	
184	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
185	
186	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
187	
188	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
189	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
190	
191	**Hard rules**:
192	
193	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
194	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
195	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
196	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
197	
198	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
199	
200	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
201	
202	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
203	
204	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
205	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
206	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
207	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
208	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
209

```

**`[keys]` built-in rebinds (lines 40-45)** — the split keys:

new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit
```
Comment (lines 37-39) stresses "Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything not listed here."

**`[[keys.command]]` custom command panes (lines 53-107)** — the tmux-popup recreations. `type = "pane"` is described (lines 47-51) as "herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`... runs from the focused pane's cwd and gets `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` / `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` / `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`." ## Findings

### 1. `create_` vs `modify_` vs plain managed — decision criteria (from `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`)

**`create_` — "seed once, then leave alone"** (lines 56-67):
> "Writes the file **only if the target does not already exist**. After that, chezmoi never touches the contents again."
> "`chezmoi add` **strips** the `create_` prefix... `chezmoi re-add`: intentionally **skips** `create_` files."
> Refresh recipe: `cp <live> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`

Use when (line 202-209, playbook section C): "Files that an app rewrites in-place after first launch, and where you only care about the initial state." Herdr is listed there explicitly (line 207): "herdr writes UI/runtime settings back into it (`onboarding = false`, theme/sound/toasts on *apply*), so a plain managed file would be clobbered every `chezmoi apply` (re-triggering onboarding)."

**`modify_` — "content is a script, not a file"** (lines 69-74):
> "The source file is an executable **script**. chezmoi pipes the current target contents into stdin; the script writes the new target contents to stdout. Lets you manage part of a file... while leaving the rest alone."

Use when (line 211-217, playbook D): "Files an app actively rewrites at runtime (adding keys, reordering, …), where you only want to enforce a subset of keys. Rule of thumb: if an app owns the file and you only care about N keys, `modify_` beats a full managed template."

**Plain managed (`dot_`)** (lines 189-194, playbook A):
> "Track normally, `chezmoi add` freely, let `chezmoi re-add` pick up drift." For everyday configs the app does not rewrite behind your back.

### 2. `CLAUDE.md` — "modify_ and create_ prefix semantics" (lines 177-182)

> - **`modify_`** files are executable scripts... **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
> - **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after... Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.

### 3. Herdr config editing / reload flow (from `docs/tools/herdr.md`)

Herdr **does** own and rewrite its config file at runtime — this is documented in the dedicated "Config writeback (why `create_`)" section (lines 145-147):
> "herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime."

Reload command: `herdr server reload-config` (lines 10, 78) — this **validates and hot-reloads** the config (reports keybind collisions in its `diagnostics`); it is a re-read, not a config-rewriting UI. The actual writeback comes from **first-run onboarding** and the **in-app settings popups**, plus `[session] resume_agents_on_restore` state. There is an onboarding "install optional agent integrations" flow (lines 132-143) but those write to `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, etc., not to `config.toml`.

The doc also spells out the propagation consequence directly (line 147):

### 1. Split-pane keybindings

# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"

# Also override default % and " so they inherit current pane's cwd (consistent with | / - and `c`)

```
bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
bind % split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
bind '"' split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
```

New window (line 304):
```
# New window/pane inherits current path
bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
```

Note: `new-session` binds do **not** set `-c` — `prefix + N` (line 310) is `command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"` and does not inherit the pane path.

---

### 3. Other notable prefix bindings ("muscle memory" standardized here)

Prefix is default **`C-b`** (no override anywhere).

**Pane navigation (vim-style), lines 226–229:**
```
bind h select-pane -L
bind j select-pane -D
bind k select-pane -U
bind l select-pane -R
```
Plus prefix-less `C-h/j/k/l` vim-tmux-navigator (lines 241–244, only when `enableVimMode` true), crossing tmux↔vim splits.

**Pane resize, lines 266–278:**
```
bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
bind -r L resize-pane -R 5
bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1
bind + resize-pane -x 75%
```

**Window / session management, lines 304–327:**
```
bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"
bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
bind M-x confirm-before -p "Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)" "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
bind M-Q confirm-before -p "Kill ALL sessions cleanly (forget auto-restore)? (y/n)" "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-server-clean.sh'"
bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane
bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
```
Note the capitalization convention: lowercase `x` = kill pane, uppercase `X` = kill session, `W` = kill window. Rename is **not** on a top-level prefix key — it lives in the right-click window/session menus (`command-prompt ... rename-window` / `rename-session`).

**Zoom:** No custom bind — relies on tmux built-in `prefix + z` (referenced in comments and exposed in menus as `resize-pane -Z`).

**Cross-session window/pane moves, lines 352–371:**
```
bind M ... choose-tree -Zs ... cross-session.sh move   (move window to another session)
bind B ... choose-tree -Zs ... cross-session.sh break  (break pane into new window in another session)
bind A ... choose-tree -Zs ... cross-session.sh link    (link window into another session)
bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"    (explode all panes into windows)
```

**Quick window switching (prefix-less, CSI-u), lines 292–301:** `C-1`…`C-9` = `select-window -t :=N`; `C-0` = sesh-root helper. Supplements built-in `prefix + 1..9`.

**Session manager (sesh) + popups, lines 391–465:**
```
bind g   -&gt; sesh fzf popup picker
bind S   -&gt; sesh last (last-session)
bind 9   -&gt; scode-here.sh (repo-aware coding-agent layout)   [overrides select-window :=9]
bind 0   -&gt; sesh-root-here.sh (lightweight session at git root)
bind T   -&gt; tv sesh popup
bind O   -&gt; sesh picker -i popup
bind U   -&gt; tv tools popup
bind a   -&gt; tv agent-panes popup
bind M-a -&gt; tv agent-wakeup popup
bind G   -&gt; lazygit popup
bind `   -&gt; one-shot shell popup
```

**Copy / capture, lines 178–220:** `prefix + y` (copy pane), `Y` (full scrollback), `C-y` (fzf line select), `C-p` (copy pane path), `M-y` (last command output, OSC 133), `M-i` (last command input). Copy-mode-vi table (lines 142–168): `v`/`V`/`C-v`/`y`, prompt navigation `{`/`}`/`M-[`/`M-]`.

**Menus / help, lines 481–550:**
```
bind ? -&gt; tmux-fzf keybinding picker (replaces default list-keys)
bind C-? -&gt; list-keys -N (fallback)
bind M-/ -&gt; glow cheatsheet popup
bind Space (and Enter unbound-&gt;) -&gt; menu.sh popup menu
bind M-p / M-w / M-s -&gt; keyboard equivalents of pane/window/status right-click menus
```

**Plugin binds (from `common.conf.tmpl`):** floax scratch pane on `prefix + F` (menu `prefix + P`); tmux-fzf-url on `prefix + u`; tmux-open `o`/`C-o`/`S` in copy-mode.

# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's

# nested. Nothing here touches the tmux / sesh / tmuxp / workmux setup.

# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
# Validate after editing: herdr server reload-config
# Full feasibility matrix + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md
#
# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true

[terminal]
shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
new_cwd = "follow"            # new panes inherit the focused pane's cwd

# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
# not listed here.
[keys]
split_vertical = "prefix+|"        # side-by-side, like tmux prefix+|
split_horizontal = "prefix+minus"  # stacked, like tmux prefix+- (also the default)
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)

# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —

[[keys.command]]

type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"

所以 `"follow"` = 「繼承 **source pane / workspace**」。這解開了矛盾:

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: deep-merge a managed overlay into ~/.codex/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: Codex CLI rewrites this file at runtime, adding per-project trust
5	# (`[projects."<absolute-path>"]`) and marketplace paths
6	# (`[marketplaces.<id>]`) that are machine-specific. Tracking the whole file
7	# would create constant diff and bake one machine's paths into another's apply.
8	# We enforce only stable preferences (personality, reasoning effort,
9	# [features], [tui.keymap.*], [plugins.*]) and round-trip the live machine
10	# state untouched. The default model is deliberately not pinned here so Codex
11	# can follow the account/CLI default unless the live config already has a
12	# user-chosen model.
13	#
14	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints
15	# the new contents on stdout. The merge runs in a small Python program because:
16	#   - jq doesn't speak TOML.
17	#   - mikefarah/yq's TOML emitter collapses nested tables into inline
18	#     `{ ... }` syntax and fails to quote keys with special characters
19	#     (e.g. `github@openai-curated`), producing invalid TOML on round-trip.
20	#   - Python 3.11+ ships `tomllib` built-in for reads; the inline writer below
21	#     handles the small schema this file uses (scalars, nested string-key
22	#     tables, no arrays-of-tables) and quotes every table key for safety.
23	#
24	# Merge precedence (later wins):
25	#   1. Stripped live (everything except [projects] and [marketplaces.*]).
26	#   2. Managed overlay (this script's $overlay heredoc).
27	#   3. Machine-local state ([projects.*], [marketplaces.*]) re-attached
28	#      verbatim so per-project trust survives an overlay churn.
29	#
30	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml
31	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (Linuxbrew/cargo-installed in the base ansible
32	# role; standard on macOS), which fetches a managed Python ≥ 3.11 if the host
33	# system python is older — guaranteeing built-in `tomllib`. Falls back to
34	# system `python3`, then to a no-op pass-through, so a fresh-bootstrap host
35	# without uv yet doesn't fail this modify_ script.
36	set -eu
37	
38	overlay=$(cat <<'TOML'
39	{{ template "agents/codex.config.overlay.toml" . }}
40	TOML
41	)
42	
43	base=$(cat)
44	
45	# Pick the python invocation. uv guarantees ≥3.11 → tomllib always
46	# importable; system python3 may be older but the script's own ImportError
47	# handler passes the live file through untouched if so. `--no-project`
48	# stops uv from picking up the dotfiles repo's pyproject.toml. `--quiet`
49	# silences "Installed X" log noise on first run.
50	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --python '>=3.11' python -
52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -
54	else
55	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; skipping merge" >&2
56	  printf '%s' "$base"
57	  exit 0
58	fi
59	
60	# Pass live file + overlay via env vars; emit merged TOML on stdout. If
61	# anything goes wrong (tomllib missing on Python <3.11, malformed live file),
62	# Python prints to stderr and exits non-zero -> chezmoi skips the file.
63	CODEX_LIVE="$base" CODEX_OVERLAY="$overlay" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
64	import os
65	import sys
66	
67	try:
68	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
69	except ModuleNotFoundError:
70	    try:
71	        import tomli as tomllib  # backport for Python 3.10 and below
72	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
73	        print(
74	            "modify_config.toml: tomllib unavailable (need Python 3.11+ or "
75	            "`pip install tomli`); skipping merge",
76	            file=sys.stderr,
77	        )
78	        sys.stdout.write(os.environ.get("CODEX_LIVE", ""))
79	        sys.exit(0)
80	
81	
82	def parse(text: str) -> dict:
83	    text = text.strip()
84	    if not text:
85	        return {}
86	    return tomllib.loads(text)
87	
88	
89	def deep_merge(base: dict, overlay: dict) -> dict:
90	    """Recursive dict merge; overlay wins on conflict. Non-dict overlay
91	    values replace base wholesale (lists are not concatenated)."""
92	    out = dict(base)
93	    for k, v in overlay.items():
94	        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
95	            out[k] = deep_merge(out[k], v)
96	        else:
97	            out[k] = v
98	    return out
99	
100	
101	def prune_reserved_builtin_providers(live: dict) -> None:
102	    """Remove invalid overrides for Codex built-in provider IDs.
103	
104	    Codex accepts `model_providers.openai.*` via one-off `-c` CLI overrides but
105	    rejects persisted config.toml files that override the reserved built-in
106	    `openai` provider. Removing the whole table repairs configs produced by
107	    the previous GFW retry experiment and any equivalent manual override.
108	    Custom provider IDs such as `openai-gfw` are left untouched.
109	    """
110	    providers = live.get("model_providers")
111	    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
112	        return
113	    providers.pop("openai", None)
114	    if not providers:
115	        del live["model_providers"]
116	
117	
118	def prune_deprecated_features(live: dict) -> None:
119	    """Drop deprecated `[features]` keys from live so they don't survive merge.
120	
121	    Codex 0.130+ renamed `codex_hooks` → `hooks`. deep_merge only replaces keys
122	    present in overlay, so without explicit removal the live `codex_hooks =
123	    true` would persist alongside the new `hooks = true` and Codex would keep
124	    emitting the deprecation warning.
125	    """
126	    features = live.get("features")
127	    if not isinstance(features, dict):
128	        return
129	    features.pop("codex_hooks", None)
130	    if not features:
131	        del live["features"]
132	
133	
134	def prune_stale_managed_model(live: dict) -> None:
135	    """Drop old model pins previously managed by this dotfiles overlay.
136	
137	    The overlay no longer pins Codex's default model; users can still keep a
138	    live `model = ...` of their own. Only remove exact stale values this repo
139	    is known to have written, so custom model choices survive the merge.
140	    """
141	    if live.get("model") in {"gpt-5.4"}:
142	        del live["model"]
143	
144	
145	def fmt_scalar(v) -> str:
146	    if isinstance(v, bool):
147	        return "true" if v else "false"
148	    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
149	        return repr(v)
150	    if isinstance(v, str):
151	        # Use basic-string with escaping. tomllib accepts both basic and
152	        # literal; basic is universal.
153	        return '"' + v.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'
154	    if isinstance(v, list):
155	        return "[" + ", ".join(fmt_scalar(x) for x in v) + "]"
156	    raise TypeError(f"unsupported scalar type for TOML emit: {type(v).__name__}")
157	
158	
159	def emit_table(prefix: str, table: dict, out: list[str]) -> None:
160	    """Emit a TOML table. `prefix` is the dotted header path (already quoted
161	    where needed); empty for root. Scalars come first, then nested tables."""
162	    scalars = {k: v for k, v in table.items() if not isinstance(v, dict)}
163	    sub = {k: v for k, v in table.items() if isinstance(v, dict)}
164	
165	    if prefix and (scalars or not sub):
166	        out.append(f"[{prefix}]")
167	    for k, v in scalars.items():
168	        out.append(f"{quote_key(k)} = {fmt_scalar(v)}")
169	    if scalars and sub:
170	        out.append("")
171	
172	    for k, v in sub.items():
173	        sub_prefix = f"{prefix}.{quote_key(k)}" if prefix else quote_key(k)
174	        emit_table(sub_prefix, v, out)
175	        out.append("")
176	
177	
178	def quote_key(k: str) -> str:
179	    """Quote any key that isn't a bare TOML key (alnum / `_` / `-` only).
180	    We over-quote rather than risk emitting invalid TOML for keys like
181	    `github@openai-curated` or absolute-path project keys."""
182	    if k and all(c.isalnum() or c in "_-" for c in k):
183	        return k
184	    return '"' + k.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
185	
186	
187	live = parse(os.environ.get("CODEX_LIVE", ""))
188	overlay = parse(os.environ.get("CODEX_OVERLAY", ""))
189	prune_reserved_builtin_providers(live)
190	prune_deprecated_features(live)
191	prune_stale_managed_model(live)
192	
193	# Pull machine-local subtrees out before merge; re-attach last so they win.
194	state = {}
195	for key in ("projects", "marketplaces"):
196	    if key in live:
197	        state[key] = live.pop(key)
198	
199	merged = deep_merge(live, overlay)
200	merged = deep_merge(merged, state)
201	
202	lines: list[str] = []
203	emit_table("", merged, lines)
204	text = "\n".join(line for line in lines if line is not None).rstrip() + "\n"
205	sys.stdout.write(text)
206	PYEOF
207
```
</details></tool-use>
