```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
23	
24	### Named sessions
25	
26	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
27	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
28	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
29	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
30	
31	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
32	
33	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
34	
35	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
38	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
39	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
40	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
41	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
42	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
43	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
44	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
45	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
46	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
47	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
48	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
49	
50	## Keybindings
51	
52	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
53	
54	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
55	
56	| Key | Action | Type |
57	|---|---|---|
58	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
59	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
60	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
61	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
62	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace nav / session navigator | built-in default |
63	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
64	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
65	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
66	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
67	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
68	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
69	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
70	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
71	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
72	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
73	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
74	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
75	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
76	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
77	
78	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
79	
80	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode`)
81	
82	Two shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion — the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` helpers. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse svibe's pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
83	
84	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
87	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
88	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
89	
90	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
91	- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
92	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
93	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
94	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
95	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
96	
97	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
98	
99	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
100	
101	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
102	
103	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
104	
105	```bash
106	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
107	```
108	
109	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
110	
111	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
112	
113	## Television integration
114	
115	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
116	
117	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
118	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
119	
120	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
121	
122	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
123	
124	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
125	
126	```bash
127	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
128	```
129	
130	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
131	
132	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
133	
134	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
135	
136	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
139	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
140	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
141	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
142	
143	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
144	
145	### Config writeback (why `create_`)
146	
147	herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime. That is why chezmoi manages it as **`create_` (seed-once)**: a plain managed file would be clobbered on every `chezmoi apply` (re-removing `onboarding=false` → the onboarding screen reappears, and reverting any UI change). Consequence: edits to `create_config.toml` in the repo do **not** auto-propagate to a machine that already has the file — refresh it deliberately with `cp ~/.config/herdr/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/herdr/config.toml)"` (then strip the runtime `onboarding`/state lines).
148	
149	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
150	
151	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
152	
153	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
154	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
155	
156	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
157	
158	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
159	
160	```bash
161	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
162	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
163	```
164	
165	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
166	
167	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
168	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
169	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
170	
171	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
172	
173	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
174	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
175	
176	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
177	
178	```bash
179	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
180	```
181	
182	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
183	
184	## AI usage / quota status
185	
186	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into. A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
187	
188	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
189	
190	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
191	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
192	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
193	
194	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
195	
196	## See also
197	
198	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
199	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)

# herdr config: tmux-parity fixes + switch `create_` → `modify_`

## Context

The herdr trial config (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml` → `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`)
has two behavior gaps vs the tmux muscle memory it's meant to mirror, and a structural
management問題 that surfaced across machines.

**Verified facts (this session):**

- herdr is really installed on the mac: `/opt/homebrew/bin/herdr` **v0.7.1**.
- **Local `diff` of source `create_config.toml` vs live `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` = 0** (in sync).
- **`david_ubuntu` live config also diffs 0 vs the same source** — config is byte-identical across machines. No chezmoi drift.
- **`david_ubuntu`: `herdr` is `NOT_ON_PATH`** even in a login shell — the Linux binary (`~/.local/bin/herdr`, devtools role) is absent, or herdr is only reached there via `herdr --remote` (which auto-installs a server binary and, by default, uses **local** keybindings + **remote** server config). So the "两台行为不同" is **not** config drift — it's a binary/version/run-mode difference, a separate thread from the config fixes below.

**Root causes of the two symptoms (both config-driven, so fixing the source fixes every host):**

1. **`prefix + %` doesn't split.** herdr's native split keys are `prefix+v` / `prefix+minus`, *not* tmux's `%` / `"`. Our config rebinds `split_vertical = "prefix+|"` (single string) and never binds `%` or `"`. tmux's `keybindings.conf.tmpl` binds **both** `|`/`%` and `-`/`"` (lines 257–263). herdr's `[keys]` **accepts arrays of bindings** (official docs example: `next_tab = ["prefix+n","ctrl+alt+]"]`), so one action can carry both keys.
2. **New tab doesn't inherit cwd.** herdr's embedded default-config comment (extracted from the binary) is authoritative:
   `# CWD policy for new panes, tabs, and workspaces …` / `# Use "follow" to inherit the source pane/workspace, "home" for $HOME, …`.
   So `new_cwd = "follow"` = "inherit the **source pane/workspace**". For a **split**, the source is the focused pane → inherits its live cwd ✓ (why splits already work). For a **new tab**, there is no same-tab source pane, so the source falls back to the **workspace**, whose cwd was pinned at startup to `$HOME` (`server log: created startup workspace cwd=/Users/daviddwlee84`) → new tab lands in `$HOME`. Candidate fix: `new_cwd = "current"` (valid values are `follow` / `home` / `current` / a path) — needs an empirical check that `current` forces the focused pane's live cwd for tabs too.

**Why `create_` (the user's question), and why we're switching.** herdr *can* own/rewrite `config.toml` at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings popups, `[session]`/`[remote]`/`[update]` state), so it was seeded once with `create_` to avoid `chezmoi apply` clobbering that writeback. The cost: **source edits never reach an already-seeded host** without a manual `cp … source-path` refresh — the structural reason keybinding tweaks feel "out of sync." (Note: on both machines the live file currently has **no** `onboarding` line and matches source exactly, so herdr's writeback is minimal/absent in practice → a managed overlay is low-risk.) **Decision (user-approved): convert to `modify_`** — a TOML-aware overlay that enforces our managed tables on every apply while preserving whatever herdr writes back. Mirrors the existing `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl` precedent.

---

## Changes

### 1. Convert `create_` → `modify_` (TOML overlay)

- `git mv dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` and rewrite it as an executable modify_ **script** (chezmoi pipes current target on stdin, script prints new contents on stdout).
- Move the desired config body (with all the header comments + tmux-parity rationale) into a template partial: **`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`** (referenced via `{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}`), matching how codex uses `.chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml`.
- **Overlay model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys** (simpler/safer than codex's strip-and-reattach because our template carries the comments):
  - Managed top-level tables we own & enforce: `theme`, `ui`, `terminal`, `keys` (incl. the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables).
  - Parse the template with **tomlkit** (preserves comments + handles array-of-tables — stdlib `tomllib` is read-only and codex's inline emitter explicitly can't emit AoT). Parse live stdin with `tomllib`. For every top-level key in live **not** in the managed set and not already in the template, copy it into the template doc (auto-preserves `onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, and any future herdr writeback). Emit `tomlkit.dumps`.
  - Python runtime guard identical to codex: `uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -` → fall back to system `python3` → **final fallback prints the raw template** (NOT stdin — on a fresh host stdin is empty, so passing it through would ship an empty config; the template keeps a python-less host fully configured, just without runtime-key preservation which doesn't exist yet on a fresh host anyway).
- `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: no change required (herdr isn't gated today). **Optional**: stat-gate the herdr config on the binary being present, so hosts like `david_ubuntu` without herdr stop getting a seeded config — list as a follow-up, don't bundle.

### 2. Split-key parity (fixes `prefix + %`)

In the managed `[keys]` block:

\```toml
split_vertical   = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]        # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux -h  (| and %)
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]   # stacked (top/bottom)     = tmux -v  (- and ")
\```

Orientation matches tmux (`%` = `-h` left/right, `"` = `-v` stacked). Validate the two shifted-punctuation tokens parse via `herdr server reload-config` diagnostics (herdr already accepts literal punctuation: `prefix+|`, `prefix+,`, `` prefix+` ``, `ctrl+alt+]`).

### 3. New-tab cwd

- Change `new_cwd = "follow"` → **`new_cwd = "current"`** and empirically verify a new tab (`prefix+c`) opens in the focused pane's live cwd (see Verification). Update the inline comment to the accurate semantics (drop the "new panes inherit the focused pane's cwd" wording, which was a guess).
- **If `current` still doesn't cover new tabs** (herdr limitation): revert to `follow` and add a workaround binding — a `[[keys.command]]` on e.g. `prefix+C` running `herdr tab create --cwd "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD"` (the CLI supports `--cwd`; command panes export `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`) — and document as a residual gap in `herdr.md`.

### 4. Full keybinding parity audit (user-requested)

Build/refresh a tmux→herdr parity table in `docs/tools/herdr.md`. Authoritative herdr action set (from the binary): `split_vertical/horizontal, focus_pane_{left,down,up,right}, swap_pane_*, cycle_pane_{next,previous}, last_pane, resize_mode, zoom, new_tab, rename_tab, previous_tab, switch_tab, close_tab, close_pane, rename_pane, copy_mode, edit_scrollback, new_workspace, workspace_picker, navigate_workspace_{up,down}, {previous,next}_workspace, new_worktree/open_worktree/remove_worktree, detach, reload_config, toggle_sidebar, remote_image_paste, indexed, command`.

| tmux binding | herdr action | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `\|`/`-`/`%`/`"` splits | `split_vertical` / `split_horizontal` | **fix → arrays** (change 2) |
| `h/j/k/l` focus pane | `focus_pane_*` (default) | keep |
| `c` new window (cwd) | `new_tab` (default `prefix+c`) | keep + change 3 (cwd) |
| `z` zoom / `x` kill pane | `zoom` / `close_pane` | keep |
| `W` kill window | `close_tab` (default `prefix+shift+x`) | **optional**: rebind `close_tab = "prefix+shift+w"` for W-parity |
| `X` kill session | `close_workspace` (session≈workspace) | optional nudge |
| `H/J/K/L` + `M-hjkl` resize | `resize_mode` (modal, `prefix+r`) | **gap** — herdr has no per-key resize outside resize-mode; document |
| swap panes | `swap_pane_*` (`prefix+shift+hjkl`) | keep |
| `R` reload | `reload_config` (`prefix+shift+r`) | keep |
| `N` new session | `new_workspace` | optional: bind for parity |
| rename (menus) | `rename_tab` (`prefix+,`) / `rename_pane` | keep |

Implement the clear win (splits). Present the `optional` rows to the user in the final report; only apply the ones they want. Record the resize-mode item as a documented gap (alongside the existing Ctrl-hjkl / OSC133 / status-glyph gaps).

### 5. Docs (CLAUDE.md cross-file rules)

- `docs/tools/herdr.md` **and its `.zh-TW` mirror**: rewrite "Config writeback (why `create_`)" → why `modify_`; update the Config bullet (line ~12) and Install/verify notes; update the keybindings table (splits row → `|`/`%` and `-`/`"`); add the `new_cwd` semantics + verdict; add resize-mode to Gaps; land the parity table from change 4.
- `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md` (~line 207): update the `create_config.toml` example → `modify_config.toml.tmpl`; herdr becomes a second `modify_` TOML precedent next to codex.
- `README.md` (~line 258): if it names the herdr config prefix, update `create_`→`modify_`.
- `CLAUDE.md` "modify_ and create_ prefix semantics": herdr now a `modify_` TOML — mention alongside codex if useful (minor).

```md
# herdr config: tmux-parity fixes + switch `create_` → `modify_`

## Context

The herdr trial config (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml` → `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`)
has a split-key gap vs tmux muscle memory, a widely-misunderstood cwd/naming model, and a
structural management issue that surfaced across machines.

**Verified facts (this session, via live herdr CLI + binary/embedded-config extraction):**

- herdr installed on both hosts (mac `/opt/homebrew/bin/herdr` v0.7.1; `david_ubuntu` reachable via interactive SSH — the earlier `NOT_ON_PATH` was a non-interactive-login PATH artifact, **not** a real absence).
- **Config is byte-identical across machines** (`diff` of source vs each host's live file = 0). No chezmoi drift. So any behavior difference between hosts is a **binary/version/run-mode** matter (e.g. `herdr --remote` uses local keybindings + remote server config), separate from the config work here.

**The real behavior model (from `herdr pane list` live data — this is what needs documenting):**

- Every pane exposes **two** cwd fields: **`cwd`** = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn) and **`foreground_cwd`** = the *live* cwd tracked via OSC7. Example observed: tab-1 root panes spawned at `$HOME` (`cwd`) but track into the project dir (`foreground_cwd`); tabs t3/t4/t5 spawned **and** stayed at `$HOME`.
- **New tabs spawn their shell at the workspace root (`$HOME`), not the focused pane's cwd.** Confirmed: every non-first tab's pane has `cwd = /Users/daviddwlee84`. This is `new_cwd = "follow"` behaving as designed (see below), *not* a bug.
- **Workspace label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (w1→`trading-journal`, w2→`chezmoi`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs doesn't — matching the user's "只有 tab 1 會關聯 space name" observation. Independent mechanism from `new_cwd`. **Decision: document only, do not change** (no config knob found for it).

**`new_cwd` semantics — authoritative (herdr's embedded default-config comment, extracted from the binary):**

\```
# CWD policy for new panes, tabs, and workspaces when no explicit --cwd is provided.
# Use "follow" to inherit the source pane/workspace, "home" for $HOME,
# "current" for Herdr's process directory, or a fixed path such as "~/Projects".
\```

So: `follow` (default) = inherit **source pane/workspace** (split→source pane ✓; new tab→the *workspace* cwd = `$HOME`). `home` = `$HOME`. **`current` = herdr's *own process* directory (NOT the focused pane) — my earlier draft's `new_cwd="current"` idea was wrong and is dropped.** **No `new_cwd` value yields "new tab in the focused pane's live cwd"** — that's only reachable via an explicit `herdr tab create --cwd …` (test-gated below).

**Split-key root cause:** herdr's native split keys are `prefix+v`/`prefix+minus`; our config rebinds `split_vertical = "prefix+|"` (single string) and never binds tmux's `%`/`"`. herdr `[keys]` **accepts arrays** (`next_tab = ["prefix+n","ctrl+alt+]"]`), so one action can carry both keys.

**Why `create_`, and why switch (user-approved → `modify_`):** herdr can rewrite `config.toml` at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings popups, `[session]`/`[remote]`/`[update]` state), so it was seeded once with `create_` to avoid clobbering. Cost: **source edits never reach an already-seeded host** without a manual refresh — the structural "out of sync" cause. (In practice both hosts' live files have no `onboarding` line and match source, so writeback is minimal → overlay is low-risk.) Convert to a **`modify_` TOML overlay** that enforces our managed tables every apply while preserving herdr's writeback, mirroring `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`.

---

## Changes

### 1. Convert `create_` → `modify_` (TOML overlay)

- `git mv dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl`; rewrite as an executable modify_ script (chezmoi pipes current target on stdin → script prints new contents).
- Move the desired config body (comments + tmux-parity rationale) into **`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`**, referenced via `{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}` (mirrors codex's `.chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml`).
- **Overlay model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:** managed top-level tables we own & enforce = `theme`, `ui`, `terminal`, `keys` (incl. the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables). Parse the template with **tomlkit** (preserves comments + emits array-of-tables — stdlib `tomllib` is read-only and codex's inline emitter can't do AoT); parse live stdin with `tomllib`; copy every top-level live key **not** in the managed set into the template doc (auto-preserves `onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, future writeback). Emit `tomlkit.dumps`.
- Runtime guard like codex: `uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -` → system `python3` → **final fallback prints the raw template** (NOT stdin: on a fresh host stdin is empty, so passthrough would ship an empty config).

### 2. Split-key parity (fixes `prefix + %`)

\```toml
split_vertical   = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]        # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux -h
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]   # stacked (top/bottom)     = tmux -v
\```

Validate the shifted-punctuation tokens via `herdr server reload-config` diagnostics (herdr already accepts literal punctuation keys: `prefix+|`, `prefix+,`, `` prefix+` ``, `ctrl+alt+]`).

### 3. New-tab cwd — **test-gated** (per user: 先實測再決定)

- Keep `new_cwd = "follow"`. **Fix the misleading inline comment** (drop "new panes inherit the focused pane's cwd") → state the real policy from the authoritative comment above.
- **Step 3a (empirical test, run first):** bind a throwaway `[[keys.command]]` (or reuse an existing command pane) that runs `echo "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD" >/tmp/herdr_probe`, `cd` into a subdir in a real pane, trigger it, and compare against that pane's `foreground_cwd` (from `herdr pane current`) vs its startup `cwd`. Confirms whether `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` is the **live** cwd.
- **Step 3b (conditional):** if 3a shows `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` = live cwd → add a `[[keys.command]]` on **`prefix+C`** running `herdr tab create --cwd "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD" --focus` (native `prefix+c` stays = workspace root). If it's the startup cwd (or the test fails) → do **not** add the binding; document new-tab-cwd as a herdr gap in `herdr.md`.

### 4. Full keybinding parity audit (user-requested)

Refresh a tmux→herdr parity table in `docs/tools/herdr.md`. Authoritative herdr action set (from binary): `split_vertical/horizontal, focus_pane_{left,down,up,right}, swap_pane_*, cycle_pane_{next,previous}, last_pane, resize_mode, zoom, new_tab, rename_tab, previous_tab, switch_tab, close_tab, close_pane, rename_pane, copy_mode, edit_scrollback, new_workspace, workspace_picker, navigate_workspace_{up,down}, {previous,next}_workspace, {new,open,remove}_worktree, detach, reload_config, toggle_sidebar, remote_image_paste, indexed, command`.

| tmux binding | herdr action | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `\|`/`-`/`%`/`"` splits | `split_vertical` / `split_horizontal` | **fix → arrays** (change 2) |
| `h/j/k/l` focus pane | `focus_pane_*` (default) | keep |
| `c` new window (cwd) | `new_tab` (default `prefix+c`) | keep; cwd via change 3 |
| `z` zoom / `x` kill pane | `zoom` / `close_pane` | keep |
| `W` kill window | `close_tab` (default `prefix+shift+x`) | **optional**: `close_tab = "prefix+shift+w"` for W-parity |
| `X` kill session | `close_workspace` (session≈workspace) | optional nudge |
| `H/J/K/L`+`M-hjkl` resize | `resize_mode` (modal, `prefix+r`) | **gap** — no per-key resize; document |
| swap panes | `swap_pane_*` (`prefix+shift+hjkl`) | keep |
| `R` reload | `reload_config` (`prefix+shift+r`) | keep |
| `N` new session | `new_workspace` | optional parity bind |
| rename (menus) | `rename_tab` (`prefix+,`) / `rename_pane` | keep |

Implement the clear win (splits). Present `optional` rows to the user; apply only what they pick. Record resize-mode as a documented gap.

### 5. Docs (CLAUDE.md cross-file rules)

- `docs/tools/herdr.md` **+ `.zh-TW` mirror**: rewrite "Config writeback (why `create_`)" → why `modify_`; update Config bullet (~line 12); update keybindings table (splits → `|`/`%` and `-`/`"`); **add a "cwd & workspace-naming model" section** (two cwd fields, new-tab spawns at workspace root, workspace label follows root-pane cwd, accurate `new_cwd` value table); add resize-mode to Gaps; land the parity table.
- `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md` (~line 207): `create_config.toml` example → `modify_config.toml.tmpl` (herdr becomes a 2nd `modify_` TOML precedent next to codex).
- `README.md` (~line 258): if it names the herdr prefix, `create_`→`modify_`.
- `CLAUDE.md` "modify_ and create_ prefix semantics": note herdr as a `modify_` TOML alongside codex (minor).

## Verification (validate-with-the-app invariant)

1. **Merge**: `chezmoi cat ~/.config/herdr/config.toml` → managed tables present, comments intact; feed a fake live file with `onboarding = false` on stdin → preserved; empty stdin → full template.
2. **Apply**: `chezmoi apply ~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (now updates the live file every run — the point of `modify_`).
3. **herdr validates**: `herdr server reload-config` → `diagnostics` show no keybind collisions / no parse error on the arrays + `new_cwd`.
4. **Splits**: `prefix+%`→left/right, `prefix+"`→stacked, `prefix+|`/`prefix+-` still work.
5. **New-tab cwd**: run test 3a; act on 3b per result.
6. **TOML lint**: `uv run --with tomlkit python -c "import tomllib;tomllib.load(open('$HOME/.config/herdr/config.toml','rb'))"` parses clean.

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- Stat-gating the herdr config on binary presence (`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`).
- The cross-host binary/version/run-mode discrepancy (config already in sync).
- workspace auto-naming behavior change (documented only, per user).

- **保留 create_,手動 refresh** - 不動管理方式。編 create_config.toml 后手動推到 live(cp / apply --force)+ herdr server reload-config。單次改動最小,但未來每次(含另一台)都要手動 refresh。

**tmux 內嵌套 herdr(多 remote)的 prefix 衝突,要怎麼解?**

Options:
- **雙擊 prefix 轉發(不改 config)** - 兩邊都保持 Ctrl+b,靠 tmux send-prefix(Ctrl+b Ctrl+b)轉發給內層 herdr。無需改 herdr config;只需確保 tmux 有 bind C-b send-prefix。最不侵入、最符 tmux 肌肉記憶。
- **改內層 herdr prefix** - 把內層 herdr keys.prefix 改成不撞 tmux 的鍵(如 ctrl+a / ctrl+space)。嵌套時直接一下進 herdr prefix;代價:單獨跑 herdr 時 prefix 也變了。

- **三種解法都只寫文件** - 不在 config 碌任何方案,只在 herdr.md 把三種解法(雙擊/改prefix/原生--remote)+ 取捨寫成一節。

```md
# herdr config: document behavior model + small parity fixes + `create_`→`modify_`

## Context

Scope (per user, converged): **primarily document herdr's real behavior model**; do a **small
muscle-memory fix** (split keys); **no forcing of cwd/workspace behavior**; add a **documented
nesting-inside-tmux** section. Convert management to **`modify_`** so edits actually propagate.

**Verified this session (live herdr CLI + binary/embedded-config extraction + web):**

- herdr on both hosts (mac `/opt/homebrew/bin/herdr` v0.7.1; `david_ubuntu` via interactive SSH — earlier `NOT_ON_PATH` was a non-interactive-login PATH artifact). **Config byte-identical across hosts** (`diff`=0) — no chezmoi drift; any cross-host behavior gap is binary/version/run-mode, not config.
- **Real cwd/naming model** (from `herdr pane list`): every pane has **`cwd`** (shell startup dir, fixed) and **`foreground_cwd`** (live, tracked via **OSC7** shell integration). New tabs spawn at the **workspace root** (`$HOME` here), *not* the focused pane's cwd. Workspace label auto-follows the **root/primary pane's** live cwd basename (`cd` in tab 1 renames the space; other tabs don't). **User insight (correct, expected):** `cd` inside a **child process / subshell** (e.g. `chezmoi cd`) doesn't emit OSC7 up to herdr, so `foreground_cwd` — and thus the space's git-repo detection and `prefix+G` lazygit location — don't update. This is inherent to OSC7 tracking; **document, don't fix.**
- **`new_cwd` authoritative values** (embedded default-config comment): `follow` = inherit source pane/workspace (default); `home` = `$HOME`; `current` = **herdr's own process dir** (NOT the focused pane — my earlier `current` idea was wrong, dropped); or a fixed path. **No value yields "new tab in focused pane's live cwd"** — only an explicit `herdr tab create --cwd …` does.
- **Split keys:** herdr native splits are `prefix+v`/`prefix+minus`; our config binds only `split_vertical = "prefix+|"`, never tmux's `%`/`"`. herdr `[keys]` **accepts arrays** → one action can carry both.
- **Nesting (herdr inside tmux):** real known conflict — outer tmux eats `Ctrl+b`, inner herdr never sees its prefix ([discussion #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)). **Confirmed: this repo's tmux keeps tmux's default `bind -T prefix C-b send-prefix` (no override/unbind), so `Ctrl+b Ctrl+b` already forwards a literal `Ctrl+b` to inner herdr — zero config change needed.** Other levers: herdr `keys.prefix` is rebindable; herdr's own double-prefix sends a literal prefix; `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` manages remotes natively without nesting; `allow_nested` (default false) is herdr-in-herdr only.
- **Why switch `create_`→`modify_`:** `create_` seeds once, so source edits never reach an already-seeded host without manual refresh (the "out of sync" cause). `modify_` overlay enforces our managed tables every apply while preserving herdr's runtime writeback. Precedent: `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`. (Both hosts' live files currently have no `onboarding` line and match source → writeback minimal → low-risk.)

---

- **Real cwd/naming model** (from `herdr pane list`): every pane has **`cwd`** (shell startup dir, fixed) and **`foreground_cwd`** (live, tracked via **OSC7** shell integration). New tabs spawn at the **workspace root** (`$HOME` here), *not* the focused pane's cwd. Workspace label auto-follows the **root/primary pane's** live cwd basename (`cd` in tab 1 renames the space; other tabs don't). **User insight (correct, expected):** `cd` inside a **child process / subshell** (e.g. `chezmoi cd`) doesn't emit OSC7 up to herdr, so `foreground_cwd` — and thus the space's git-repo detection and `prefix+G` lazygit location — don't update. ```toml
# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator.
#
# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other (or
# nest deliberately; see docs/tools/herdr.md "nested inside tmux"). Nothing here
# touches the tmux / sesh / tmuxp / workmux setup.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves any keys herdr writes back at
# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [update] / [experimental]).
#
# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
# Validate after editing: herdr server reload-config
# Full feasibility matrix + behavior model + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md
#
# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).
#
# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true

[terminal]
shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
# NOTE: a split's source is the focused pane (→ inherits its live cwd), but a
# NEW TAB's source is the WORKSPACE root, so new tabs open at the workspace cwd
# (often $HOME), NOT the focused pane's live cwd. No new_cwd value changes that;
# for "new tab here" use `herdr tab create --cwd …`. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
new_cwd = "follow"

# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
[keys]
split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)

# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+G"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+`"
type = "pane"
command = "$SHELL"
description = "scratch shell (popup pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+U"
type = "pane"
command = "tv tools"
description = "CLI tools launcher (tv tools)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+T"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-sesh"
description = "Session / workspace / dir switcher (herdr-aware tv channel)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+a"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-agent-panes"
description = "Live agent panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+f"
type = "pane"
command = "tv fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts SSH picker (tv)"

# --- herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + popup-menu analog) ---
# Requires: herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus
# Projects = declarative multi-pane workspace templates (see
# dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/).
# Quick Actions = fuzzy command launcher. If the plugin is not installed these
# bindings simply no-op.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+O"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects"
description = "herdr-plus: Projects (layout launcher)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+y"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions"
description = "herdr-plus: Quick Actions"

```tmpl
#!/bin/sh
# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
#
# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
# new contents on stdout.
#
# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
#
# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
# round-trips both.
#
# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
set -eu

template=$(cat <<'TOML'
{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
TOML
)

live=$(cat)

if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- python3 -
else
  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$template"
  exit 0
fi

HERDR_TEMPLATE="$template" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
import os
import sys

# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
        sys.stdout.write(os.environ.get("HERDR_TEMPLATE", ""))
        sys.exit(0)

# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
try:
    import tomlkit
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print(
        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    sys.stdout.write(os.environ.get("HERDR_TEMPLATE", ""))
    sys.exit(0)

MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}

template_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_TEMPLATE", "")
live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()

doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}

# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
for key, value in live.items():
    if key in MANAGED:
        continue
    if key in doc:
        continue
    doc[key] = value

sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
PYEOF

```

The lone backtick confuses the parser into thinking it's starting an old-style command substitution, then it searches for the closing backtick and hits EOF instead. This is a known quirk in bash where backticks inside `$(...)` can be misparsed even when they're in quoted heredocs, because backtick scanning happens at a different lexer stage than quote handling.

The real solution is to avoid capturing the template in a variable using `$(cat <<'TOML' ... TOML)` altogether. The backtick issue only occurs when the heredoc body is inlined into the script text within a `$(...)`. When capturing runtime data like `live=$(cat)`, the backtick comes from stdin data, not from the script text itself, so that's fine.

I'll pass the template file path to Python via an environment variable and read it there, which sidesteps all shell backtick issues entirely. The fallback is just `cat "$tmpfile"` to output the raw template.

# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
#
# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
# new contents on stdout.
#
# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
#
# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
# round-trips both.
#
# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
#
# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
set -eu

tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM

cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
TOML

live=$(cat)

if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- python3 -
else

  cat "$tmpl_file"
  exit 0

HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
import os
import sys

tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
    template_text = fh.read()


def emit_template():
    sys.stdout.write(template_text)


# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
        emit_template()
        sys.exit(0)

# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.

except ModuleNotFoundError:

        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,

live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}

for key, value in live.items():

=== head of rendered ===
# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator.
#
# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other (or
# nest deliberately; see docs/tools/herdr.md "nested inside tmux"). Nothing here
# touches the tmux / sesh / tmuxp / workmux setup.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves any keys herdr writes back at
# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [update] / [experimental]).
#
# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
# Validate after editing: herdr server reload-config
# Full feasibility matrix + behavior model + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md
#
# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).
#
# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true

[terminal]
shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
# NOTE: a split's source is the focused pane (→ inherits its live cwd), but a
# NEW TAB's source is the WORKSPACE root, so new tabs open at the workspace cwd
# (often $HOME), NOT the focused pane's live cwd. No new_cwd value changes that;
# for "new tab here" use `herdr tab create --cwd …`. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
new_cwd = "follow"

# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---

56:split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)

The overlay uses a Python script with tomlkit to merge the managed template (which enforces the core tables like `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[keys]`) with any runtime-written keys from the live file, so herdr's changes survive `chezmoi apply`. This solves the sync problem where repo edits never reached already-seeded machines. The script degrades gracefully if tomlkit isn't available, falling back to system Python or just emitting the raw template.

Now I'm adding a section explaining how herdr tracks working directories differently from tmux: each pane has both a startup `cwd` (fixed at spawn) and a `foreground_cwd` (live, updated via OSC 7 shell integration), and `cd` commands inside subshells that don't re-emit OSC 7 won't propagate to herdr's tracking, so git detection and lazygit location won't follow — that's an OSC 7 limitation, not a herdr issue.

New tabs always spawn at the workspace root rather than the focused pane's directory, even though splits inherit the focused pane's cwd. The workspace label auto-follows the primary pane's live directory basename, so `cd` in tab 1 renames the space, but `cd` in other tabs doesn't trigger that. The `new_cwd` config option controls where new panes and tabs open — it can be set to `follow` (default, inheriting from source), `home`, `current` (herdr's own process directory), or a fixed path. To open a new tab in the focused pane's current directory, I'd need to explicitly bind a command that passes `--cwd "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD"` to `herdr tab create`.

When nesting herdr inside tmux, the prefix collision is the main issue since both default to `Ctrl+b`. The cleanest solution is using tmux's built-in `send-prefix` to forward `Ctrl+b Ctrl+b` to the inner herdr, letting its prefix bindings work normally without any configuration changes. Alternatively, I could rebind the inner herdr's prefix to something like `Ctrl+a` or `Ctrl+space` to avoid the collision entirely, though that requires one extra keystroke.

For multiple remote servers, herdr's native `--remote` flag might be simpler than nesting — it runs a local client against a remote herdr server without tmux in between. I should note that tmux's root-table bindings shadow inner-app `Ctrl` keys, so reaching herdr actions through its prefix is more reliable than trying direct terminal shortcuts.

177	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
178	
179	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
180	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
181	
182	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
```

212	
213	Files an app actively rewrites at runtime (adding keys, reordering, …), where you only want to enforce a subset of keys.

220
